subject: Dedicated capacity sizing deep-dive — scheduling and throughput details
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@nebulahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing deep-dive — scheduling and throughput details

Hi Samantha / Tom,

Thanks again for the discovery call earlier — great to learn more about NebulaHealth's telemetry and where you want to embed model-driven summarization into the clinician workflow. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can scope Dedicated capacity correctly: 

Recap (from our call)
- Primary workload: clinical note summarization + short Q&A in the EHR sidebar.
- Typical request size: ~300 tokens in, ~150 tokens out; some bursts up to 1,000 tokens for batched report generation.
- Expected concurrency: 30 steady, spikes to ~150 during morning rounds.
- 95th p50 latency target: <= 250ms for single-turn interactions; background batch can be higher.
- Data residency: US-east preferred; SOC2 / HIPAA discussed.

What we need from you to size Dedicated accurately
- Target steady-state qps / RPS and peak qps during spikes (approx numbers are fine).
- Desired 95th latency SLO for interactive flows and acceptable tail for batch.
- Preferred model family (open model or any constraints on quantized variants).
- Any requirements around GPU type (A100 vs H100) or deployment zone.

Proposed next step: 60-minute technical deep-dive (Dedicated capacity sizing) where our infra engineer will walk through throughput/latency trade-offs and we can validate sample traces. Can you do one of these slots next week (all times PDT):
- Mon 2026-05-25 09:00–10:00
- Tue 2026-05-26 11:00–12:00
- Wed 2026-05-27 14:00–15:00

If none work, tell me two times that do and I will coordinate. I’ll invite Dev (cc’d) from our infra team — he’ll want access to a small workload sample (or a sanitized request log) ahead of the call if possible.

Attached: current infra snapshot you shared during the call (I pulled out the bullet points).

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0193

From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@nebulahealth.com>

Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@nebulahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 18:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing deep-dive — scheduling and throughput details

Hey Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with what we saw. Quick answers below, and we can lock a slot after a quick internal sync: 

Answers:
- Steady qps: ~10–15 for sidebar interactions; peak qps during rounds: ~120–160 (30–40 clinicians, some batched requests kicking off).
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 300ms is ideal; p99 below 1s would be great if achievable.
- Model: leaning toward an open 7B or 13B family; we are open to quantized variants if the quality tradeoff is acceptable.
- GPUs: no hard constraint, but we prefer cost-effective options; if H100 gives a clear latency benefit at scale we can discuss.
- Residency: US-east is primary, but we need a secondary region for failover (US-west).

Tom and I are free Tue 2026-05-26 11:00–12:00 PDT — that slot works. I attached an internal infra snippet (sanitized) so your infra team can preview concurrency patterns.

Regards,
Samantha Li
Director of Platform Engineering, NebulaHealth
samantha.li@nebulahealth.com
(617) 555-0110
